title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: Herzog asks Eisenkot to form a government
stories.summary: President Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming Israel's next government. Eisenkot got recommendations from 67 Knesset members vs 46 for Netanyahu; he has 28 days. No coalition locked yet.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.why: Domestic power fight; no global-control shift yet.
stories.what_it_means: Israel is sorting who runs the country after a hung vote — a domestic fight, not a global handoff.
stories.economic_impact: Markets and aid partners will watch for a stable cabinet vs another election.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a co-op board picking a chair with no clear majority.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Riyadh; Aramco tower damaged
stories.summary: Iran-backed Houthis launched missiles and drones at the Saudi capital. Debris/strike damage hit an Aramco tower; Saudi side said damage was minor, no deaths.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Iran-backed group using a capital and oil offices as leverage.
stories.what_it_means: A group tied to Tehran is using another country's capital and oil offices as leverage.
stories.economic_impact: Insurance and Gulf shipping risk stay elevated; Brent was near about $93 Monday.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a gang throwing fireworks at the bank to scare the street.

stories.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya
stories.summary: COP31 opened Monday in Antalya, Türkiye (Nov 9–20). Nearly 200 countries bargaining over energy, farm and finance rules. Nothing binding on day one.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: Nearly 200 nations bargain energy and finance rules in one UN room.
stories.what_it_means: Energy, farm and finance choices for almost 200 nations are bargained again in one UN room.
stories.economic_impact: Any finance or fossil language that sticks later can move fuel costs and farm rules worldwide.
stories.everyday_example: It's like landlords rewriting everyone's lease in one hall.

stories.headline: Trump: postwar Ukraine will have a different shape
stories.summary: Trump told 60 Minutes a Ukraine deal is close and Ukraine will end up with a "little bit different shape." U.S.–Russia–Ukraine talks set for Abu Dhabi Nov 10–11. Deal terms undisclosed.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: Great powers sketching Ukraine's map before Ukrainians lock terms.
stories.what_it_means: Bigger powers are sketching Ukraine's map before Ukrainians agree.
stories.economic_impact: Ceasefire odds swing Europe's defense and energy budgets; markets will price whatever Abu Dhabi leaks.
stories.everyday_example: It's like two landlords redrawing your walls before you've signed.

stories.headline: Iran destroys Hormuz navigation aids; claims route halted
stories.summary: IRGC told Iranian state media navigational aids on Hormuz southern rocks were destroyed and the unauthorized southern route is fully halted. Claims not independently verified. Brent fell about 5% to roughly $93.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: One government gating a shared energy route.
stories.what_it_means: Iran is still treating a shared world energy lane as its private gate.
stories.economic_impact: Brent near multi-week lows on peace hopes, but shipping and insurance stay expensive at a gated chokepoint.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighbor smashing the streetlights on the road to the store.
